title: The Hilbert polynomial
statement:
Let $X$ be a proper scheme of dimension $g$ over a field $k$
and $\mathcal M$ an ample invertible
$\mathcal O_X$-module. Then $m\mapsto\chi(X,\mathcal M^{\otimes m})$
is a numerical polynomial in $m$ of total degree at most $g$, the
*Hilbert polynomial* of $\mathcal M$.
(*Source: Stacks Project, Varieties, Lemma 33.45.1, Tag
[0BEM](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BEM).*)

proof.text: Prove the stronger assertion by induction on $d=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)$: for every coherent $\mathcal F$ on a proper scheme and every invertible $\mathcal M$, $m\mapsto\chi(X,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal M^{\otimes m})$ is numerical of degree at most $d$. Apply [lem-sc-hilbert-embedded-points] to obtain $0\to\mathcal K\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'\to0$, with equal support, no embedded points for $\mathcal F'$, and smaller support for $\mathcal K$; tensoring remains exact because $\mathcal M$ is invertible, and [lem-pc-euler-additive] reduces the assertion for $\mathcal F$ to the induction assertion for $\mathcal K$ and the quotient $\mathcal F'$. Reduce the latter to its scheme-theoretic support $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$: [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-support] gives $i$ with image $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F')$, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence] writes $\mathcal F'=i_*G$, and [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology] identifies the cohomology after tensoring with $G\otimes i^*\mathcal M$. Since $G$ is faithful on $Z$, locally $\mathcal O_Z$ embeds in a finite direct sum of copies of $G$, so $\operatorname{Ass}(\mathcal O_Z)\subseteq\operatorname{Ass}(G)$; as $G$ has no embedded associated points and $\operatorname{Supp}(G)=Z$, all associated points of $Z$ are generic. Thus $Z$ has no embedded points and $G$ has no embedded points with support $Z$, so we may replace $X,\mathcal F'$ by $Z,G.

source.place: Tag 0BEM, induction on the dimension of the support and reduction to the support

proof.text: For the reduced situation, the preceding support argument gives a locally Noetherian scheme $X$ with no embedded points and a coherent sheaf $\mathcal F'$ with no embedded points and support $X$. Then [lem-sc-regular-meromorphic-section-exists] supplies a regular meromorphic section of $\mathcal M$. Apply [lem-sc-hilbert-difference] with $\mathcal L=\mathcal M$: its cokernels $\mathcal Q,\mathcal Q'$ are coherent of support dimension $<d$, and [lem-pc-euler-additive] gives the displayed identity for the forward difference of $P_{\mathcal F'}(m)=\chi(X,\mathcal F'\otimes\mathcal M^{\otimes m})$. The induction hypothesis applies to $\mathcal Q$ and $\mathcal Q'$ (using the same support reduction), so $P_{\mathcal F'}(m+1)-P_{\mathcal F'}(m)$ is numerical of degree at most $d-1.

source.place: Tag 0BEM, proof after the embedded-point reduction

proof.text: When $d=0$, [lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support] identifies Euler characteristics and their invertible twists, so $P_{\mathcal F}$ is constant. For $d>0$, summing the numerical-polynomial forward difference and fixing one value of $P_{\mathcal F}$ gives a numerical polynomial of degree at most $d$; this is the elementary finite-difference induction in Tag 0BEM. Finally take $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ and $d=\dim X=g$ to obtain the stated Hilbert polynomial.

source.place: Tag 0BEM, induction base and final arithmetic argument

lean.statement:
theorem Scheme.Hom.exists_polynomial_hilbertFunction (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [IsProper f]
    (M : X.Modules) (hM : IsAmple f M) :
    ∃ P : Polynomial ℚ, P.natDegree ≤ ((topologicalKrullDim X).unbotD 0).toNat ∧
      ∀ m : ℕ, P.eval (m : ℚ) = f.hilbertFunction M m :=
lean.note: The upstream theorem states the Hilbert polynomial assertion exactly: for a proper scheme over a field and an ample module, there is a rational polynomial of degree at most the topological Krull dimension agreeing with the Euler-characteristic Hilbert function on every natural m.
